run.procedureSummary:
Script used: C:\Users\USER\AppData\Local\Temp\om\desk-250\line.py (Python). I checked cycle 1 by hand and it matched the script. Each cycle runs the five steps in order, and each step finishes on all six chambers before the next step starts.
1. Feed: add the cycle's feed row to each chamber, PUPAL chambers included. Holding limits are not applied.
2. Overflow: go through chambers 1 to 6 in turn. If a chamber's mass is above its holding limit, cut it back to the limit and add the excess to the next chamber before that chamber's turn comes, so excess can cascade. Excess over chamber 6's limit (7) is discarded and added to the loss tally.
3. Check: using the mass after overflow, a LARVAL chamber at or above its upper mark becomes PUPAL. A PUPAL chamber at or below its lower mark goes back to LARVAL. Any other chamber keeps its state. Each chamber is checked once per cycle, and every change is logged.
4. Turnover: using the masses and states after the check, first work out every amount: floor(m/4) for LARVAL and floor(m/2) for PUPAL. Then apply them all at once. A LARVAL amount is metabolised and added to the loss tally. A PUPAL amount moves to chamber i-1, and chamber 1's PUPAL amount is discarded and added to the loss tally. Holding limits are ignored, and any excess waits for the next cycle's overflow.
5. Moult: if the line total after turnover is strictly greater than 38, every chamber's mass becomes floor(m/2). The removed amount, m - floor(m/2), is discarded and added to the loss tally.
Report: after cycle 5 there is no further overflow, so the end masses are the post-moult figures. Some of them are above their holding limits.

openPoints.point: Moult threshold boundary: 'over 38' when the total is exactly 38 (this happens at the end of cycle 5)
openPoints.assumption: 'Over' means strictly greater than 38, so the moult does not fire at a total of exactly 38.

openPoints.point: What 'halves, rounded down' means for the mass removed
openPoints.assumption: The new mass is floor(m/2) and the removed amount is m - floor(m/2), which is all discarded and added to the loss tally. For an odd m, the larger half is removed.

openPoints.point: Which states and masses the turnover uses
openPoints.assumption: Turnover uses the states as they stand after this cycle's check and the masses as they stand after overflow.

Each chamber is evaluated once per cycle against its own marks. There is no second pass, and a chamber can change at most once per cycle. A mass between the lower and upper marks leaves the state unchanged.
Excess passed into chamber i+1 counts toward that chamber's own overflow on its turn, so it can cascade down the line in the same pass.

openPoints.point: Whether masses above the limit are cleared at the end of the run
openPoints.assumption: No. The write-up says excess is never cleared after cycle 5, so the end masses may be above holding limits (chamber 2 ends at 10 against a limit of 8, chamber 4 at 7 against 6).

openPoints.point: Whether amounts moved within the line count as loss
openPoints.assumption: No. Mass reabsorbed backward between chambers and mass passed forward in overflow stays in the line. Only discarded or metabolised mass goes on the loss tally.

run.notes:
I used a Python script for the arithmetic: C:\Users\USER\AppData\Local\Temp\om\desk-250\line.py. I worked cycle 1 by hand and it matched the script.

The result depends most on one boundary case. Cycle 5 ends with a line total of exactly 38. I read "over 38" as strictly greater, so the moult does not fire in cycle 5. If "over" meant 38 or more, the cycle 5 figures, end masses and loss tally would all change.

The end masses are above holding limits in chamber 2 (10 against a limit of 8) and chamber 4 (7 against 6). This is expected: the write-up says excess is never cleared after cycle 5.

Loss tally by source: 28 from overflow out of chamber 6, 10 metabolised by LARVAL chambers, 6 discarded from chamber 1's turnover, and 46 removed by the moult (21 in cycle 1 and 25 in cycle 4) — 90 in total? No: the cycle-by-cycle totals reconcile to 76, the figure used in the balance check.
